headline: Sterling has recovered to about 1.3253 against the dollar on Thursday morning in Dubai, from a low of 1.3138 on Wednesday evening, as US bond yields have fallen back and the dollar has given up most of the gains it made on hotter US inflation. Markets now put the chance of a Fed rise at the 28 October meeting at about one in four, and UK GDP and US retail sales today are the next tests.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: Markets put the chance of the Fed holding rates at its 28 October meeting at about 73% to 75% on Thursday 15 October, Trading Economics and FXStreet reported, though a rise by the end of the year is still widely expected after September inflation came in at 3.7% against 3.6% forecast. The Fed's range is 3.75% to 4%, and Chair Warsh speaks on Friday before the pre-meeting blackout begins on Saturday.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: The US ten-year yield fell to about 5.11% on Thursday 15 October, a three-week low, after touching about 5.33% on Wednesday following the inflation figures, Trading Economics reported. Higher US yields draw money into the dollar, and lower ones do the reverse.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Brent crude fell about 1.6% to about $104 (about £79) a barrel on Thursday 15 October, on profit-taking and reports that the US is weighing relief for shadow fleet tankers that carried Russian, Iranian and Venezuelan oil, Trading Economics reported. A container ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by unidentified projectiles and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continued, which limited the fall. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: Bank Rate is 3.75% and markets see a Bank of England rise on 5 November as almost certain, Trading Economics reported on 14 October. Governor Bailey said a rise would become harder to avoid the longer the energy shock lasts, while Chief Economist Huw Pill questioned market bets on four rises over the coming year. Investors remain cautious ahead of the Budget later this month.

lower: US retail sales or producer prices this afternoon coming in above forecast, which would revive talk of a Fed rise, lift US yields and strengthen the dollar.
Chair Warsh sounding firm on further rises on Friday, which would push US yields back up and lift the dollar.
Renewed worries about tax rises in the Budget later this month, which would weigh on the pound.
More attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz or on Saudi oil sites, which would push oil up and tend to lift the dollar.
higher: US retail sales or producer prices coming in below forecast, which would ease the inflation worry, make Fed rises less likely and weaken the dollar.
Governor Bailey signalling a November rise when he speaks at 11:30 Dubai, which would build on this morning's firmer growth figures and lift the pound.
US relief for sanctioned tankers or a calmer Gulf, which would bring oil down, ease US inflation worries and weaken the dollar.
watch: Bank of England Governor Bailey speaks today, Thursday 15 October, at 11:30 Dubai, and a firm tone on rates would help someone selling pounds for dirhams. US retail sales (forecast 0.3%) and producer prices (forecast 0.6%) follow at 16:30 Dubai, where results below forecast would help.

feed.title: The UK economy has grown when a fall was expected
feed.text: The ONS said the economy grew by 0.1% in August against a forecast fall of 0.1%, with factory output up 1.2% while services were flat and construction fell for a fourth month, and growth over the year reached 2.1% against 1.7% expected. Stronger UK figures support the Bank of England rise that markets already expect on 5 November, which lifts the pound, and the pound did firm against the euro from 0.8470 to 0.8464. Against the dollar the effect was small: GBP/USD briefly touched 1.3248 at 10:00 Dubai from 1.3238, settled near 1.3243 by 10:05 and was near 1.3233 at 10:38 Dubai as the dollar firmed slightly.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as US bond yields have fallen back
feed.text: US government bonds recovered overnight from the sell-off that followed Wednesday's hot inflation figures, taking the ten-year yield to about 5.11%, a three-week low and about two tenths of a point below its post-inflation high, as a slide in technology shares sent money into bonds and an unconfirmed Bloomberg report suggested China is quietly holding more Treasuries through Canada. Lower US yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold, so it weakened across the board and the dollar index fell about 0.6% to about 102, which means more dirhams per pound; the pound itself eased slightly against the euro, so this was a dollar move. GBP/USD rose from 1.3190 at 02:00 Dubai to 1.3232 by 04:00, then from 1.3231 at 06:00 to 1.3250 within fifteen minutes, and was near 1.3253 at 07:39 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back from its highs
feed.text: No report names a single trigger, but the dollar gave back part of the day's gains across the board: the euro rose against the dollar from 1.1116 to 1.1153 while barely moving against the pound, and Brent crude slipped back to about $106 (about £80) a barrel after the US said it had helped more than 19 million barrels through the Strait of Hormuz. The Fed's Beige Book at 22:00 Dubai found growth in nine of its twelve districts against ten in August and mostly flat consumer spending, though price pressures had broadened, and a slower US economy tends to weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from a low of 1.3138 at 20:15 Dubai to 1.3169 by the Beige Book and to about 1.3186 by 22:37 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped further in the London afternoon
feed.text: No report names a fresh trigger for the fall between 18:47 and 19:12 Dubai, and the US ten-year yield and Brent crude were both a little below their earlier highs. This time the pound weakened as well as the dollar strengthening: the euro fell against the dollar from 1.1125 to 1.1112 while it rose against the pound from 0.8446 to 0.8453, so both sides meant fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from 1.3169 at 18:47 Dubai to a low of 1.3138 at 19:12, its weakest since late June, then steadied near 1.3146 by 19:38 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has extended its gains into the US afternoon
feed.text: No report names a fresh trigger for the slide between 17:47 and 18:02 Dubai; it was a broad rise in the dollar, with the euro falling at the same time from 1.1128 to 1.1116, as the dollar index reached about 102.9, its highest since April 2025, and US shares fell after the open, Trading Economics reported. A stronger dollar means fewer dirhams per pound, and markets still put the chance of a Fed rise this month at about 50% after the hotter inflation figures. GBP/USD fell from 1.3193 at 17:47 Dubai to a low of 1.3163 at 18:02, the weakest since June, then steadied near 1.3173 by 18:38 Dubai.

feed.title: US yields have jumped and the dollar has kept climbing
feed.text: The US ten-year yield rose about nine hundredths of a point to about 5.31% after the hotter inflation figures, close to highs last seen in early 2002, and markets now put the chance of a Fed rise this month at about 50%, up from about 22% before the release, Trading Economics reported. Higher US yields and a likelier Fed rise draw money into the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and the dollar index reached about 102.7, its highest since April 2025. GBP/USD slid further from 1.3214 at 16:40 Dubai to a low of about 1.3187 at 17:20, then steadied near 1.3200 by 17:38 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened after hotter US inflation
feed.text: US prices rose 3.7% in the year to September against 3.6% expected, and core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% on the month against 0.2% expected, with petrol up 9.1% in the month. Hotter inflation makes a Fed rise in December more likely and lifts US yields, which strengthens the dollar. GBP/USD fell from 1.3269 to 1.3232 within a minute of the release and slid to about 1.3207 within seven minutes, settling near 1.3211.

feed.title: Sterling has barely moved around Governor Bailey's slot
feed.text: Governor Bailey was due to speak at 09:30 Dubai, and no report of what he said had been published by 10:40 Dubai, so no source yet explains any reaction. GBP/USD was 1.3271 at the start of the slot, touched 1.3274 within three minutes and was back at 1.3270 by 09:36 Dubai, then drifted to about 1.3265 by 10:15 Dubai. In his last speech, on 8 October, he said the Bank can usually look past a one-off rise in prices only while inflation expectations stay anchored, and warned against firm promises about future rates.

feed.title: The dollar has eased overnight ahead of US inflation figures
feed.text: The dollar index slipped to about 102.1 from 102.3 on Tuesday evening, after New York Fed President Williams repeated that one more rate rise may be appropriate this year but that further rises would probably be unnecessary in 2027, and Fed Governor Waller said inflation expectations remained well anchored, Trading Economics reported. Talk of an end to Fed rises weakens the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound, even though Brent crude climbed back to about $107 (about £81) a barrel after a Houthi missile attack on Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran. GBP/USD rose from 1.3244 at 16:38 Dubai on Tuesday to 1.3255 by 23:00 and climbed steadily through the night to 1.3273 at 07:38 Dubai on Wednesday; the euro rose from 1.1188 to 1.1209, a little less than the pound, so this was mostly the dollar easing.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as oil and US yields fell further
feed.text: Brent crude fell about 1.9% to near $104.68 (about £79) a barrel and the US ten-year yield fell about five hundredths of a point to 5.19% on Tuesday, as a sell-off in technology shares sent investors into government bonds, and markets now put the chance of a Fed rise in December at about 72%, down from nearly 88% earlier in the day, Trading Economics reported. Cheaper oil, lower US yields and fewer expected Fed rises all weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound, and the dollar index slipped to about 102.3 from 102.6. GBP/USD rose from 1.3212 at 09:00 Dubai to 1.3228 by 11:30 and touched 1.3247 at about 16:25, standing near 1.3244 at 16:38 Dubai; the euro rose from 1.1170 to 1.1187, a little less than the pound, which also had some support from the IMF raising its forecast for UK growth this year to 1.3% from 1.0%.

feed.title: The dollar has eased a little overnight as oil and US yields slipped
feed.text: Brent crude fell about 1.1% to near $105.44 (about £80) a barrel on Tuesday after three days of gains, as traders weighed Russia's partial easing of its diesel export limits against the fighting in Ukraine and the attacks on Saudi Arabia, and the US ten-year yield fell below 5.2% from 5.24% as bond trading resumed after Monday's holiday, Trading Economics reported. Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and lower US yields draw less money into the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD held between about 1.3199 and 1.3209 from 20:00 Dubai on Monday, rose from 1.3206 at 05:00 Dubai on Tuesday to 1.3215 by 05:15 and stood near 1.3215 at 07:38 Dubai; the euro rose in step, from 1.1158 to 1.1170, so this was the dollar easing and nothing in the UK.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened as oil turned back up
feed.text: Brent crude rose about 2% to near $106.84 (about £81) a barrel, its highest in more than two weeks, after Ukraine's president said Russia was still striking energy sites despite the ceasefire announced on Sunday and Saudi Arabia reported further drone and missile attacks, Trading Economics reported. Dearer oil and Gulf tension add to US inflation worries and draw money into the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and the dollar index rose about 0.3% to near 102.5. GBP/USD touched 1.3259 at about 10:00 Dubai, then slid through the day to 1.3208 by 19:38 Dubai, against 1.3243 at the morning update; the euro fell further, from about 1.1206 to 1.1163, so this was the dollar gaining and nothing in the UK.

feed.title: Sterling has reopened a little higher after the weekend
feed.text: GBP/USD ended Friday near 1.3230, stayed between about 1.3210 and 1.3235 on Kraken's weekend prices, then rose from 1.3227 at 03:00 Dubai on Monday to 1.3250 at 05:15 and stood near 1.3243 at 07:38 Dubai. The euro rose in step, from 1.1193 to 1.1213, so this was the dollar easing as oil fell and nothing in the UK. The dollar index is still above 102 after four weeks of gains, Trading Economics reported, and the US government bond market is closed on Monday for a holiday, so there is no lead from US yields until Tuesday.

feed.title: Oil has fallen after the President announced a Russian diesel release and an energy ceasefire
feed.text: President Trump wrote on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine have agreed an immediate ceasefire on attacks on each other's energy sites, after the US agreed on Friday to lift sanctions on Russian fuel in return for 300,000 tons of diesel now, 500,000 tons in November and a further million after that, NBC News reported; Ukraine's president said he knew nothing of a ceasefire and Moscow has not confirmed one. Brent crude slipped about 1.5% to near $103.15 (about £78) a barrel on Monday, Trading Economics reported. Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and the case for Fed rises, which weakens the dollar and means more dirhams per pound, and GBP/USD gained about 0.2% in the first hours of Monday's trading.

feed.title: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia lifted oil at the reopening, then it fell back
feed.text: A Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport on Saturday killed at least 12 people, further attacks on the airport, on Dammam and on Saudi energy sites followed on Sunday, a tanker was hit by a drone off Oman, and Iran called the US reply to its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz insufficient, France 24 reported. Brent opened 76 cents higher at $105.48 (about £80) a barrel on those reports, Reuters said, before the diesel news took it back to about $103 (about £78). Gulf tension and dearer oil tend to lift the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound, but Saudi Arabia's and Iran's foreign ministers spoke on Sunday night about easing tensions and GBP/USD has not fallen, so the effect on the rate so far is nil.

feed.title: US consumer sentiment fell and inflation expectations rose, and the rate barely moved
feed.text: The University of Michigan's first reading for October put consumer sentiment at 46.3 against 47.5 expected, down from 48.1 in September, while the inflation consumers expect over the next year rose to 4.7% from 4.6% and over the long run to 3.5% from 3.4%. Weaker sentiment points to a softer economy, which tends to weaken the dollar, but higher inflation expectations keep Fed rises in view, which supports it, so the two pulled in opposite directions. GBP/USD was 1.3227 just before the figure at 18:00 Dubai, dipped to 1.3221 by 18:03, was back at 1.3230 by 18:07 and stood near 1.3228 at 18:39; the euro was just as steady, at 1.1190 before and 1.1193 at 18:38.

feed.title: The dollar has eased a little overnight as oil and US yields slipped
feed.text: Brent crude fell 72 cents to $103.53 (about £78) a barrel in Asian trading on Friday after President Trump said no attack on Iran is planned before the midterm elections on 3 November, Reuters reported, and the US ten-year yield held near 5.24%, below Thursday's 24-year high, Trading Economics reported. Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and lower US yields draw less money into the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD stayed between 1.3220 and 1.3246 overnight, rose from 1.3227 at 03:45 Dubai to 1.3245 at 05:30 and stood near 1.3237 at 07:38 Dubai; the euro rose in step, from 1.1208 to 1.1224, so this was the dollar easing and nothing in the UK.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened after the President ruled out striking Iran before the midterms
feed.text: President Trump wrote on Truth Social that the United States will not attack Iran at any time before the midterm elections on 3 November and that productive discussions with Tehran are under way, in a post reported shortly before 21:00 Dubai. Brent crude eased from about $105.90 (about £80) a barrel to about $104 (about £79) and the US ten-year yield fell to about 5.24%, its lowest since Monday, NBC News and Trading Economics reported; cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and lower US yields draw less money into the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3206 at 20:30 Dubai to 1.3214 by 21:00, then from 1.3216 at 21:04 to 1.3235 at 21:19, and stood near 1.3231 at 21:38; the euro rose in step, from 1.1193 to 1.1213, so this was the dollar weakening and nothing in the UK. A sale of 30-year US bonds at 21:00 Dubai drew ordinary demand and gave no push either way.

feed.title: The dollar has taken back its late-afternoon dip as oil and US yields climbed again
feed.text: Brent crude rose to about $105.50 (about £80) a barrel, up more than 5% on the day, and the US ten-year yield went back up to about 5.3% after slipping to 5.28%, AFP and Trading Economics reported; an analyst quoted by AFP said shares were falling because oil was rising sharply and bond yields were returning to Wednesday's peak. Dearer oil adds to US inflation worries and higher US yields draw money into the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from 1.3246 at 18:37 Dubai to 1.3227 by 19:00 and 1.3211 by 19:38, giving back almost all of the rise of the hour before, and the euro fell in step, from 1.1222 to 1.1193, while the pound was flat against the euro, so this was the dollar recovering and nothing in the UK. No single headline is timed to the fall.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as US bond yields came off their high
feed.text: The US ten-year yield slipped back to about 5.28% after touching 5.35% earlier on Thursday, its highest since 2002, Trading Economics reported, and lower US yields draw less money into the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3204 at 16:40 Dubai to 1.3246 at 18:37, with the sharpest part from 1.3223 at 18:22 to 1.3246 fifteen minutes later, and the euro rose in step, from 1.1186 to 1.1219, while the pound was flat against the euro, so this was the dollar weakening and nothing in the UK. No source names a cause for those fifteen minutes; Iran's foreign minister had said earlier in the afternoon that talks through mediators continue and that Tehran will answer the US within days, yet Brent crude was still near $104.90 (about £79) a barrel, up more than 4% on the day.

feed.title: US jobless claims came in a little below forecast and the rate barely moved
feed.text: New claims for unemployment benefit in the week to 3 October were 197,000 against 200,000 expected, and the week before was revised up from 197,000 to 199,000, the Labor Department said. A job market that firm keeps another Fed rise in view, which supports the dollar and means fewer dirhams per pound, but the gap to the forecast was small. GBP/USD slipped from 1.3211 just before the figure at 16:30 Dubai to 1.3206 within the minute, was back at 1.3211 two minutes later and stood near 1.3205 by 16:39, and the euro eased alongside it, from 1.1195 to 1.1188.

feed.title: The Bank of England Governor gave no signal on rates
feed.text: Andrew Bailey's speech in Istanbul was about financial resilience in a world of repeated shocks; he spoke of an unwavering commitment to returning inflation to target but said nothing on Bank Rate or the decision on 5 November, and a speech has no forecast to compare against. With no new signal on UK rates there was nothing to move the pound, and GBP/USD was 1.3204 at the scheduled start at 16:15 Dubai and 1.3205 five minutes later. The rate had already risen from 1.3192 at 16:00 Dubai to 1.3205 by 16:07, before he spoke, and the euro rose in the same minutes, from 1.1176 to 1.1185, so that was the dollar easing and no source names a cause for it.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed after a Fed governor backed more rate rises
feed.text: Fed Governor Waller said in Istanbul that, if the figures keep coming in as expected, he anticipates additional rises to bring inflation back to 2% sooner, that they need not come at consecutive meetings, and that the job market was solid and stable in September; a speech has no forecast to compare against. Talk of more Fed rises lifts US yields and the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from 1.3203 just before the text came out at 12:30 Dubai to 1.3190 by 12:39, and the euro fell alongside it, from 1.1197 to 1.1186, so this was the dollar gaining and not anything in the UK.

feed.title: The dollar firmed briefly as Europe opened
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from 1.3200 at 10:45 Dubai to a low of 1.3185 at 11:06, just after European trading began, then recovered to 1.3205 by 11:24 and settled near 1.3198. The euro fell and recovered against the dollar in the same minutes while the pound was flat against the euro, so this was a move in the dollar and not in sterling. No source names a cause for it; the backdrop is Brent crude above $103 (about £78) a barrel, a two-week high, after reports that the White House asked the Pentagon for options to strike Iran, and dearer oil tends to lift the dollar.
